column1: w: 1.~I've been a wild rover for many's the year, ~ and I've spent all my money on
w: whiskey and beer. But now I'm returning with gold in great store ~ and I
w: never will play the wild rover no more and it's No, Nay, Never! ~ No nay
w: never no more ~ will I play ~ the wild rover. ~ No, never, ~ no more
W: I went into an alehouse I used to frequent
W: and I told the landlady my money was spent.
W: I asked her for credit, she answered me nay,
W: Such a custom like yours I can have any day
W: I took from my pocket ten sovereigns bright
W: and the landlady's eyes opened wide with delight.
W: She said ""you'll have whiskey and wines of the best
W: and the words that I told ye were only in jest.""
W: I'll go home to my parents, confess what I've done,
W: and I'll ask them to pardon their prodigal son.
W: And when they've caressed me as oft' times before
W: then I never will play the wild rover no more"

column1: w: 1.~A_ black-smith court-ed_ me, nine_ months and bet-ter._ He_
w: fair-ly won my_ heart, wrote_ me a let-ter._ With his
w: Ham-mer in_ his_ hand, he_ looked quite cle--ver,_ and if
w: I were with my_ love, I'd_ live_ for-e-ver._
W: But where is my love gone with his cheeks like roses?
W: He's gone across the sea gathering primroses.
W: I'm afraid the scorching sun will shine and burn his beauty,
W: And if I was with my love I'd do my duty.
W: Strange news is come to town, strange news is carried.
W: Strange news flies up and down that my love is married.
W: I wish them both much joy although they cannot hear me.
W: And may God reward him well for the slighting of me.
W: Don't you remember when you lay beside me?
W: And you said you'd marry me and not deny me?
W: If I said I'd marry you it was only for to try you,
W: So bring your witness love and I'll not deny you.
W: No, witness have I none save God Almighty,
W: And may he reward you well for the slighting of me.
W: Her cheeks grew pale and wan it made her poor heart tremble,
W: To think she loved that one and he proved deceitful."

column1: w: 1.~I've been a wild rover for many's the year, ~ and I've spent all my money on
w: whiskey and beer. But now I'm returning with gold in great store ~ and I
w: never will play the wild rover no more and it's No, Nay, Never! ~ No nay
w: never no more ~ will I play ~ the wild rover. ~ No, never, ~ no more
W: I went into an alehouse I used to frequent
W: and I told the landlady my money was spent.
W: I asked her for credit, she answered me nay,
W: Such a custom like yours I can have any day
W: I took from my pocket ten sovereigns bright
W: and the landlady's eyes opened wide with delight.
W: She said ""you'll have whiskey and wines of the best
W: and the words that I told ye were only in jest.""
W: I'll go home to my parents, confess what I've done,
W: and I'll ask them to pardon their prodigal son.
W: And when they've caressed me as oft' times before
W: then I never will play the wild rover no more"

column1: W: When all but dreaming was Fanny Power,
W: A light came streaming from out her bower.
W: A heavy thought at her door delayed.
W: A heavy hand on the latch was laid.
W: ""Now, who dare venture at this dark hour
W: Unbid to enter my maiden bower?""
W: ""Oh, Fanny, open the door to me
W: And your true lover you'll surely see.""
W: ""My own true lover so tall and brave,
W: He lives in next isle o'er the angry wave.""
W: ""Your true love's body lies on the pier.
W: His faithful spirit is with you here.""
W: ""Oh, his look was cheerful and his voice was gay,
W: Your face is fearful and your speech is gray;
W: And sad and tearful your eye of blue.
W: Ah, but Patrick, Patrick, alas, 'tis you!""
W: The dawn was breaking. She heard below
W: The two cocks shaking their wings to crow.
W: ""Oh, hush you! hush you! both red and gray,
W: Or will you hurry my love away?""
W: ""Oh, hush your crowin', both gray and red,
W: Or he will be goin' to join the dead;
W: And cease you calling his ghost to the mold;
W: And I'll come crowning your wings with gold.""
W: When all but dreaming was Fanny Power,
W: A light came streaming beneath her bower;
W: And on the morrow, when they awoke,
W: They knew that sorrow her heart had broke.

column1: W: When all but dreaming was Fanny Power,
W: A light came streaming from out her bower.
W: A heavy thought at her door delayed.
W: A heavy hand on the latch was laid.
W: ""Now, who dare venture at this dark hour
W: Unbid to enter my maiden bower?""
W: ""Oh, Fanny, open the door to me
W: And your true lover you'll surely see.""
W: ""My own true lover so tall and brave,
W: He lives in next isle o'er the angry wave.""
W: ""Your true love's body lies on the pier.
W: His faithful spirit is with you here.""
W: ""Oh, his look was cheerful and his voice was gay,
W: Your face is fearful and your speech is gray;
W: And sad and tearful your eye of blue.
W: Ah, but Patrick, Patrick, alas, 'tis you!""
W: The dawn was breaking. She heard below
W: The two cocks shaking their wings to crow.
W: ""Oh, hush you! hush you! both red and gray,
W: Or will you hurry my love away?""
W: ""Oh, hush your crowin', both gray and red,
W: Or he will be goin' to join the dead;
W: And cease you calling his ghost to the mold;
W: And I'll come crowning your wings with gold.""
W: When all but dreaming was Fanny Power,
W: A light came streaming beneath her bower;
W: And on the morrow, when they awoke,
W: They knew that sorrow her heart had broke.

column1: W: When all but dreaming was Fanny Power,
W: A light came streaming from out her bower.
W: A heavy thought at her door delayed.
W: A heavy hand on the latch was laid.
W: ""Now, who dare venture at this dark hour
W: Unbid to enter my maiden bower?""
W: ""Oh, Fanny, open the door to me
W: And your true lover you'll surely see.""
W: ""My own true lover so tall and brave,
W: He lives in next isle o'er the angry wave.""
W: ""Your true love's body lies on the pier.
W: His faithful spirit is with you here.""
W: ""Oh, his look was cheerful and his voice was gay,
W: Your face is fearful and your speech is gray;
W: And sad and tearful your eye of blue.
W: Ah, but Patrick, Patrick, alas, 'tis you!""
W: The dawn was breaking. She heard below
W: The two cocks shaking their wings to crow.
W: ""Oh, hush you! hush you! both red and gray,
W: Or will you hurry my love away?""
W: ""Oh, hush your crowin', both gray and red,
W: Or he will be goin' to join the dead;
W: And cease you calling his ghost to the mold;
W: And I'll come crowning your wings with gold.""
W: When all but dreaming was Fanny Power,
W: A light came streaming beneath her bower;
W: And on the morrow, when they awoke,
W: They knew that sorrow her heart had broke.

column1: W: When all but dreaming was Fanny Power,
W: A light came streaming from out her bower.
W: A heavy thought at her door delayed.
W: A heavy hand on the latch was laid.
W: ""Now, who dare venture at this dark hour
W: Unbid to enter my maiden bower?""
W: ""Oh, Fanny, open the door to me
W: And your true lover you'll surely see.""
W: ""My own true lover so tall and brave,
W: He lives in next isle o'er the angry wave.""
W: ""Your true love's body lies on the pier.
W: His faithful spirit is with you here.""
W: ""Oh, his look was cheerful and his voice was gay,
W: Your face is fearful and your speech is gray;
W: And sad and tearful your eye of blue.
W: Ah, but Patrick, Patrick, alas, 'tis you!""
W: The dawn was breaking. She heard below
W: The two cocks shaking their wings to crow.
W: ""Oh, hush you! hush you! both red and gray,
W: Or will you hurry my love away?""
W: ""Oh, hush your crowin', both gray and red,
W: Or he will be goin' to join the dead;
W: And cease you calling his ghost to the mold;
W: And I'll come crowning your wings with gold.""
W: When all but dreaming was Fanny Power,
W: A light came streaming beneath her bower;
W: And on the morrow, when they awoke,
W: They knew that sorrow her heart had broke.

column1: w: 1.~I've been a wild rover for many's the year, ~ and I've spent all my money on
w: whiskey and beer. But now I'm returning with gold in great store ~ and I
w: never will play the wild rover no more and it's No, Nay, Never! ~ No nay
w: never no more ~ will I play ~ the wild rover. ~ No, never, ~ no more
W: I went into an alehouse I used to frequent
W: and I told the landlady my money was spent.
W: I asked her for credit, she answered me nay,
W: Such a custom like yours I can have any day
W: I took from my pocket ten sovereigns bright
W: and the landlady's eyes opened wide with delight.
W: She said ""you'll have whiskey and wines of the best
W: and the words that I told ye were only in jest.""
W: I'll go home to my parents, confess what I've done,
W: and I'll ask them to pardon their prodigal son.
W: And when they've caressed me as oft' times before
W: then I never will play the wild rover no more"

w: whiskey and beer. But now I'm returning with gold in great store ~ and I
w: never will play the wild rover no more and it's No, Nay, Never! ~ No nay
w: never no more ~ will I play ~ the wild rover. ~ No, never, ~ no more

W: and I told the landlady my money was spent.
W: I asked her for credit, she answered me nay,
W: Such a custom like yours I can have any day
W: I took from my pocket ten sovereigns bright
W: and the landlady's eyes opened wide with delight.
W: She said ""you'll have whiskey and wines of the best
W: and the words that I told ye were only in jest.""
W: I'll go home to my parents, confess what I've done,
W: and I'll ask them to pardon their prodigal son.
W: And when they've caressed me as oft' times before
W: then I never will play the wild rover no more"

column1: w: 1.~I've been a wild rover for many's the year, ~ and I've spent all my money on
w: whiskey and beer. But now I'm returning with gold in great store ~ and I
w: never will play the wild rover no more and it's No, Nay, Never! ~ No nay
w: never no more ~ will I play ~ the wild rover. ~ No, never, ~ no more
W: I went into an alehouse I used to frequent
W: and I told the landlady my money was spent.
W: I asked her for credit, she answered me nay,
W: Such a custom like yours I can have any day
W: I took from my pocket ten sovereigns bright
W: and the landlady's eyes opened wide with delight.
W: She said ""you'll have whiskey and wines of the best
W: and the words that I told ye were only in jest.""
W: I'll go home to my parents, confess what I've done,
W: and I'll ask them to pardon their prodigal son.
W: And when they've caressed me as oft' times before
W: then I never will play the wild rover no more"

W: A light came streaming from out her bower.
W: A heavy thought at her door delayed.
W: A heavy hand on the latch was laid.
W: ""Now, who dare venture at this dark hour
W: Unbid to enter my maiden bower?""
W: ""Oh, Fanny, open the door to me
W: And your true lover you'll surely see.""
W: ""My own true lover so tall and brave,
W: He lives in next isle o'er the angry wave.""
W: ""Your true love's body lies on the pier.
W: His faithful spirit is with you here.""
W: ""Oh, his look was cheerful and his voice was gay,
W: Your face is fearful and your speech is gray;
W: And sad and tearful your eye of blue.
W: Ah, but Patrick, Patrick, alas, 'tis you!""
W: The dawn was breaking. She heard below
W: The two cocks shaking their wings to crow.
W: ""Oh, hush you! hush you! both red and gray,
W: Or will you hurry my love away?""
W: ""Oh, hush your crowin', both gray and red,
W: Or he will be goin' to join the dead;
W: And cease you calling his ghost to the mold;
W: And I'll come crowning your wings with gold.""
W: When all but dreaming was Fanny Power,
W: A light came streaming beneath her bower;
W: And on the morrow, when they awoke,
W: They knew that sorrow her heart had broke.

column1: w: 1.~I've been a wild rover for many's the year, ~ and I've spent all my money on
w: whiskey and beer. But now I'm returning with gold in great store ~ and I
w: never will play the wild rover no more and it's No, Nay, Never! ~ No nay
w: never no more ~ will I play ~ the wild rover. ~ No, never, ~ no more
W: I went into an alehouse I used to frequent
W: and I told the landlady my money was spent.
W: I asked her for credit, she answered me nay,
W: Such a custom like yours I can have any day
W: I took from my pocket ten sovereigns bright
W: and the landlady's eyes opened wide with delight.
W: She said ""you'll have whiskey and wines of the best
W: and the words that I told ye were only in jest.""
W: I'll go home to my parents, confess what I've done,
W: and I'll ask them to pardon their prodigal son.
W: And when they've caressed me as oft' times before
W: then I never will play the wild rover no more"

w: ~ and I spent all my mon--ey- ~~on whis-key and beer.
w: But now I'm re-turn-ing with gold in great store ~

W: and I told the landlady my money was spent.
W: I asked her for credit, she answered me nay,
W: Such a custom like yours I can have any day
W: I took from my pocket ten sovereigns bright
W: and the landlady's eyes opened wide with delight.
W: She said ""you'll have whiskey and wines of the best
W: and the words that I told ye were only in jest.""
W: I'll go home to my parents, confess what I've done,
W: and I'll ask them to pardon their prodigal son.
W: And when they've caressed me as oft' times before
W: then I never will play the wild rover no more"
